lines.li: [us] What does a day in the company look like when there's no fighting?
[them,their:lowtech] Drill at dawn with pike and crossbow, then mending, then more drill.
[them] Drill at dawn, then cleaning the guns, then more drill.
[us] Every day?
[them] Every day, a company that stops drilling is just a crowd with weapons.
[us] What does the company eat on the march?
[them] Hard bread, salt pork and whatever the contract says the town must provide.
[us] And when the town doesn't provide it?
[them] Then the paymaster writes it down, and the town pays for it later.
[us] Are there children in the company?
[them] Some, they stay in the home town with the baggage while we're out on a contract.
[us] Do they grow up to be soldiers too?
[them] Most do, but nobody draws the company's pay before sixteen, that's the rule.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A barracks with a town around it, and a quartermaster's store bigger than the chapel.
[us] Does anyone live there who isn't a soldier?
[them] The families, the smiths and the sutlers, and they all work for the company.
[us] Does the company take sides between the peoples here?
[them,their:war] Only when paid, but {WAR} are at war with us, so that one is our own fight.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] We made peace with {PEACEWITH} lately, so they'll be hiring again soon.
[them,!their:war] Never, we fight for whoever pays, and just now nobody's at war with us.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] We're on bad terms with {WAR} ourselves.
[us,their:war] I hope it ends soon for your sake.
[us,!their:war] That sounds like a quiet season for you.
[them,their:war] It ends when one side stops paying for it, that's how wars go.
[them,!their:war] Quiet seasons are when the company mends its boots.
[us] What does a soldier make of our colony?
[them,likesus] A place I'd sign a contract with, if the terms were fair.
[them,wary] I'd want my wage paid in advance before I stood guard here.
[them] Fair ground, and I've already worked out where I'd post the sentries.
[us] That's a soldier's way of looking at things.
[them] It's the only way I have, it's habit.
[us] What does a day of listening look like?
[them] We sit in the quiet halls around the Spire and write down what we hear.
[us] What do you hear?
[them] The hum, mostly, and on the days it's louder we write more.
[us] What do the Choir eat?
[them] Plain food, bread and broth and fruit, nothing with a strong taste.
[us] Why not?
[them] A plain meal doesn't distract you while you're listening, we say.
[us] Do your children hear the hum too?
[them] Each generation born near the Spire hears a little more of it than the last.
[us] Is that a good thing?
[them] We think so, though some of the young ones find it hard to sleep.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] Rings of quiet halls around a monolith, and nobody raises their voice.
[us] Not even the children?
[them] The children are allowed to, the halls can bear a little noise.
[us] How do the Choir get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] Badly with {WAR} just now, though we fight as little as we can.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] Better with {PEACEWITH} now, and the halls are glad of the quiet after a war.
[them,!their:war] Well, we trade them psychic things for art and keep out of their quarrels.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] {WAR} are no friends of ours either.
[us,their:war] I hope it stays far from your halls.
[us,!their:war] I'm glad things are calm for you.
[them,their:war] We hope it stays far away, a battle is very loud to people like us.
[them,!their:war] So are we, it leaves more time for listening.
[us] What does the Choir make of our colony?
[them,likesus] It's a kind sort of noise here, people talking and working, I like listening to it.
[them,wary] It's loud here, and I find it hard to listen.
[them] Busy, and I like listening to an ordinary day.
[us] You're welcome to stay a while.
[them] Thank you, I'll keep out of everyone's way.
[us] What's a shift like down the shaft?
[them] Ten hours at the face, then up for air with the next shift coming down.
[us] Who decides who works which shift?
[them] We vote on it, like everything else, and it's all written in the book.
[us] What do miners eat at Deepwell?
[them] Pasties, mostly, a whole meal you can carry down the shaft in your pocket.
[us] Are they any good?
[them] After ten hours at the face, they're the best thing you'll ever taste.
[us] Do your children go down the mine?
[them] Not before they're grown, the union voted on that years ago.
[us] What do they do until then?
[them] School in the union hall, and every one of them learns to read the book.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A shaft, a headframe, the union hall and rows of houses all the same.
[us] Will it stay there?
[them] As long as the seam lasts, and when it runs out we vote on where to go.
[us] How does the union get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] Badly with {WAR}, and every shift talks of nothing else.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] Better with {PEACEWITH} since the peace, and the members are glad of it.
[them,!their:war] Well enough, we sell to anyone who pays the price the members agreed.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] We've had our own trouble with {WAR}.
[us,their:war] I hope it ends soon.
[us,!their:war] Then I'm glad things are quiet for you.
[them,their:war] The members want it over, but it isn't only up to us.
[them,!their:war] So are we, quiet means full shifts.
[us] What does a miner think of our colony?
[them,likesus] You work hard here, I can tell, and you don't seem to mind it.
[them,wary] I'd like to know who decides things here, and whether anyone asks the rest.
[them] Good ground, I'd like to know what's under it.
[us] That's honest of you.
[them] The union doesn't waste words, we've too much digging to do.
[us] What does a broker do all day?
[them] Listens to the ships above, then to the towns below, and writes down the difference.
[us] The difference?
[them] What one will pay and the other will sell for, that's what we live on.
[us] What do people eat at the enclave?
[them] Whatever came down on the last ship, so it's different every week.
[us] That sounds interesting.
[them] It is, and expensive, and some weeks it's all tinned fish.
[us] How are the enclave's children raised?
[them] On the pads, among the cargo, learning to count before they can read.
[us] Count what?
[them] Crates and prices, and later what a promise is worth.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A landing pad with a market around it, open every hour a ship might land.
[us] Is it ever quiet?
[them] Between ships, for an hour or so, and everyone sleeps then.
[us] How does the enclave get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] With {WAR}, badly, and that is bad for business.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] With {PEACEWITH}, better since the peace, and their account is open again.
[them,!their:war] We trade with everyone, so we can't afford to quarrel with anyone.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] We're not on good terms with {WAR} either.
[us,their:war] I hope it doesn't cost you too much.
[us,!their:war] Good for business, I imagine.
[them,their:war] Everything costs something, and we'll write it in the manifest.
[them,!their:war] Very good, and we'd like it to stay that way.
[us] What does a broker make of our colony?
[them,likesus] A good account to hold, and I'd like it to stay that way.
[them,wary] A risk, until I see how you deal.
[them,small] Small, but small accounts grow.
[them] Interesting, I'm still working out what you have to sell.
[us] We'll keep that in mind.
[them] Please do, the enclave remembers every account.
[us] What does a sequencer do in a day?
[them] Reads, mostly, the ledger and the samples, and changes very little.
[us] I thought you'd be changing genes all day.
[them] One change a season is a busy season, and every one goes in the ledger.
[us] What do the Works eat?
[them] Vat-grown food, mostly, since that's what we're good at, and the garden gives us the rest.
[us] Does it taste like anything?
[them] It tastes like food, though the garden's apples are better.
[us] Do your children have their genes chosen for them?
[them] Never, they choose their own when they're old enough to understand.
[us] And until then?
[them] They grow up as they were born, and plenty decide to stay that way.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A gene lab with a vat hall, and a quiet garden where the vats can't be heard.
[us] Why a garden?
[them] The founders had one, and we've kept it as they left it.
[us] How do the Works get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] {WAR} are at war with us, which we never asked for.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] Better with {PEACEWITH} since the peace, and they've started selling us samples again.
[them,!their:war] Well enough, people come to us for medicine, whatever they think of the vats.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] We've had trouble with {WAR} too.
[us,their:war] I'm sorry to hear it.
[us,!their:war] I'm glad to hear it.
[them,their:war] We'd treat their wounded all the same, if they asked us.
[them,!their:war] So are we, the vats need quiet years.
[us] What do the Works make of our colony?
[them,likesus] Good people, as far as I can tell, and that counts for more than genes.
[them,wary] I'd want to know how you treat people who are different from you.
[them] Interesting, I'd like to know how you keep everyone healthy.
[us] We try to look after each other.
[them] That works better than most things in the ledger.
[us] What does a herder's day look like?
[them] Out with the herd at first light, back at dusk for the count.
[us] And in between?
[them] Watching the grass and the sky, and keeping the dogs busy.
[us] What do your people eat?
[them] Milk, curd and meat, and bread when we trade for flour.
[us] Do you eat your own herd?
[them] Only the old and the lame, the rest are counted.
[us] When do your children start herding?
[them] As soon as they can walk behind a goat.
[us] That young?
[them] Tamsa was a girl when she drove the herd north, so we start them early.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] Round houses and pens, and in a month it will be somewhere else.
[us] Don't you miss staying in one place?
[them] The grass doesn't stay, so neither do we.
[us] How do the herding folk get on with the others?
[them,their:war] Badly with {WAR}, we keep the herd close and the spears closer.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] Better with {PEACEWITH} now, the pastures are shared again.
[them,!their:war] Well, anyone who doesn't steal from the herd is welcome at the pot.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] We don't trust {WAR} either.
[us,their:war] Keep the herd safe, then.
[us,!their:war] Then the grass is good for everyone.
[them,their:war] The herd is counted every night, and that won't change.
[them,!their:war] This year it is, and we're glad of it.
[us] What do you make of our colony?
[them,colony:animals] You keep animals, so we have something to talk about.
[them,likesus] Good people, I'd share a pot with you.
[them] You stay in one place, and I'd find that hard, but you look settled.
[us] Come back any time.
[them] We will, when the grass brings us this way.
[us] What does the crew do all day, if the ship never flies?
[them] We keep the watches, check the systems and write the log.
[us] What goes in the log?
[them] Most days, that the ship is holding position, and that's a good day.
[us] What does the crew eat?
[them] Ship's rations, the same recipe since the voyage, and a garden in the cargo hold.
[us] Two hundred years of the same recipe?
[them] It's a good recipe, and changing it would need the captain's order.
[us] Are your children crew too?
[them] Every child is entered in the log at birth and given a post at twelve.
[us] What kind of post?
[them] The one their parent held, mostly, so the watches stay filled.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] It's the hull, with a few things built around it that aren't ship.
[us] Is the ship comfortable to live in?
[them] It was built for a voyage, not a life, but we've made it do.
[us] How does the Fleet get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] {WAR} are hostile, and the ship is at its battle stations.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] The log shows peace with {PEACEWITH} now, and the watch has been eased.
[them,!their:war] Correctly, we trade with them and keep to our posts.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] {WAR} are no friends of ours either.
[us,their:war] I hope the hull holds.
[us,!their:war] That sounds very orderly.
[them,their:war] The hull was built for worse than them, and it's held for two hundred years.
[them,!their:war] It is, and order is most of what we have.
[us] What does the crew make of our colony?
[them,likesus] A well-run post, if you'll take that as the compliment it is.
[them,wary] I'd need to see your log before I could say.
[them] You've built a lot on the ground, which none of us ever learned to do.
[us] You'd be welcome to look around.
[them] Thank you, I'll note it in the log.
[us] What does a day in the guild look like?
[them] Kiln lit before dawn, work until the light goes, and the mark on whatever's finished.
[us] Do you mark everything?
[them] Everything, so anyone can find us if it breaks.
[us] What does the guild eat?
[them] Bread baked in the kilns' heat, and a stew that sits by the forge all day.
[us] That sounds good.
[them] It is, and the bread has the baker's mark on it too.
[us] How does someone join the guild?
[them] As an apprentice at twelve, and a journeyman after seven years.
[us] And then?
[them] A year among other peoples, and only then a master with a mark of your own.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] Kilns, forges and a carved guildhall, and the best-built houses in the region.
[us] You'd say that, though.
[them] I would, and the marks on the stones would back me up.
[us] How does the guild get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] We're at war with {WAR}, and the forges are making weapons instead of hinges.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] Well enough with {PEACEWITH} since the peace, and we're glad to be making hinges again.
[them,!their:war] Well, everyone needs good work done, and they come to us for it.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] {WAR} have caused us trouble too.
[us,their:war] That's a waste of good smiths.
[us,!their:war] That's a good position to be in.
[them,their:war] We'll be glad to get back to honest work when it's over.
[them,!their:war] It is, as long as the work stays good.
[us] What does a guild mason make of our colony?
[them,likesus] There's honest work here, and I'd say so to the guild.
[them,wary] I'd want to see who built your roofs before I slept under them.
[them] I've been looking at how you build, out of habit.
[us] And what do you think?
[them] Some of it's good and some isn't, and the guild always says so plainly.
[us] What does a Lattice mechanitor do all day?
[them] Tend the mechs, check the links, and charge whoever needs charging.
[us] Don't you get tired of them?
[them] No, working with them feels like working with friends.
[us] Do your people eat like everyone else?
[them] Plain meals, at the same hour, and we eat together so nobody eats alone.
[us] Is that important?
[them] A mind left on its own is what we fear most, so yes.
[us] Are your children linked to the mechs?
[them] Not until they're grown and ask for it, the link is for life.
[us] What do they do before then?
[them] Learn to repair what the mechs break, which keeps them very busy.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A charging yard, a gestation hall and a control tower, and mechs everywhere.
[us] Isn't it noisy?
[them] It hums, and after a while you only notice when it stops.
[us] How does the Lattice get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] {WAR} are at war with us, and the mechs are on watch day and night.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] We made peace with {PEACEWITH}, and the war mechs are resting.
[them,!their:war] Quietly, we repair their mechs and buy their subcores.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] {WAR} are no friends of ours either.
[us,their:war] I hope the watch holds.
[us,!their:war] A quiet arrangement.
[them,their:war] The mechs don't sleep, so the watch will hold.
[them,!their:war] We prefer it, most of us are quiet people.
[us] What does the Lattice make of our colony?
[them,likesus] People here look out for each other, which we respect.
[them,wary] Everyone here thinks alone, and that would worry me.
[them] Busy, and I've been counting how many hands a few mechs would save you.
[us] We do things our own way here.
[them] So you do, I'm only saying what a Lattice would notice.
[us] What does a carter's day look like on the road?
[them] Up before light, everything loaded and checked, and as far as we can get before dark.
[us] Every day?
[them] Every day the road's open, and a waystation at the end of it if we're lucky.
[us] What do carters eat on the road?
[them] Whatever the waystation's cooking, and it's usually beans.
[us] Every night?
[them] Every night, and a waymaster who serves anything else gets good ink in the Book.
[us] Do your children travel with the caravans?
[them] From the cradle, most of them, and they know the road better than the maps do.
[us] Do they ever settle?
[them] Some stay on to keep a waystation, and the rest keep moving.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A walled waystation where two roads meet, with stables, a store and beds.
[us] Is it busy?
[them] Busy enough that the waymaster never sleeps more than four hours.
[us] How does the league get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] We're at war with {WAR}, so our caravans go the long way round them.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] {PEACEWITH} are at peace with us again, and the road through their land is open.
[them,!their:war] We carry for everyone, so we keep the road open between all of them.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] We'd give {WAR} red ink in our book too.
[us,their:war] That must cost you some trade.
[us,!their:war] Open roads are good for everyone.
[them,their:war] The long way costs us, but a caravan that's robbed costs more.
[them,!their:war] They are, and keeping them open is the league's whole business.
[us] What does the league make of our colony?
[them,likesus] Good ink, as far as I'm concerned, and I'd say so to the waymaster.
[them,wary] I haven't decided what ink you deserve yet.
[them] A stop worth making, if the road brings us this way.
[us] We'll try to deserve good ink.
[them] Deal fairly, and you won't have to try.
[us] What does a grove-keeper do all day?
[them] Counts the trees, plants the seedlings and walks the edge of the grove for fallen wood.
[us] Counts them?
[them] Every tree cut and every tree planted, near and far, so the count stays even.
[us] What do the Mossborn eat?
[them] Nuts, berries, mushrooms and roots, and meat when the hunters are lucky.
[us] Do you farm?
[them] We plant, but only trees, and the rest the forest gives us.
[us] How are your children raised?
[them] Every child plants a tree when they can first hold a trowel, and tends it as they grow.
[us] What happens to the tree?
[them] It grows beside them all their life, and it's the one they're buried near.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A grove of living trees, with our houses among the roots and the dead under the saplings.
[us] Don't you cut any wood at all?
[them] Only what has fallen, or what we've already paid for with a seedling.
[us] How do the Mossborn get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] {WAR} are at war with us, and a war always costs the forest.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] At peace with {PEACEWITH} now, and we've begun planting where the fighting was.
[them,!their:war] Patiently, we think better of the ones who plant than the ones who only clear.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] {WAR} have troubled us too.
[us,their:war] I hope it ends before many trees are lost.
[us,!their:war] That sounds like a patient way to live.
[them,their:war] A forest takes a long time to grow back, so we hope it ends soon.
[them,!their:war] It's the only way, trees don't hurry.
[us] What do the Mossborn make of our colony?
[them,likesus] You're good neighbors, and our elders speak well of you.
[them,wary] The count will tell us what kind of neighbors you are.
[them] I've been looking at your trees, and how many there are.
[us] We try to be fair to the land.
[them] Then the count will show it, in time.
[us] What's a day like in one of the order's sickhouses?
[them] Rounds at dawn, rounds at noon, rounds at dusk, and the lamp lit at nightfall.
[us] And in between?
[them] Washing, boiling, mending and writing names in the Book of the Spared.
[us] What does the order eat?
[them] Broth, bread and whatever the patients don't finish.
[us] That doesn't sound like much.
[them] It's enough, and the patients come first.
[us] Do children ever join the order?
[them] Some we nursed as children come back when they're grown and take the vows.
[us] Why do they come back?
[them] We were spared, and so we owe, they say, and they mean it.
[us] What is {TOWN} like?
[them] A sickhouse with a town around it, and a lamp over every door.
[us] Does anyone sleep there?
[them] The patients do, mostly, and the rest of us take turns.
[us] How does the order get on with the other peoples?
[them,their:war] {WAR} are at war with us, and we'll still nurse their wounded if they come.
[them,their:peace,!their:war] Since the peace with {PEACEWITH}, our wards have room again.
[them,!their:war] We take in anyone who comes to the door, so we try to be no one's enemy.
[us,their:war,war:ourfoe] {WAR} have done us no kindness either.
[us,their:war] That's more than most would do.
[us,!their:war] Your work never stops, does it?
[them,their:war] Aldith let raiders in, and we keep her lamp.
[them,!their:war] It doesn't, but the lamp stays lit.
[us] What does the order make of our colony?
[them,likesus] Good people, the sort who'd open the door at night.
[them,wary] I'd like to know what you do with the wounded raiders.
[them] Busy, and I hope your sick are well looked after.
[us] We do our best.
[them] That's all the order asks of anyone.
